body.statement: Suppose \(\mathsf C=1\) and the returned reconstruction has a continuously differentiable local extension \(F\) at \(o\) with finite derivative. Then \(F(\widehat o_n)\to Q\) in probability and \(\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-Q\}\Rightarrow N(0,DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top)\). The same result holds for inverse-probability audit tables after composing with their fixed known-\(e\) linear map.
body.justification: Regular branches of the constructive reconstruction yield estimators and a joint limit law without pretending that rank-changing branches are smooth.
body.gap: Levis et al. transform a full-data influence function after complete follow-up; the derivative here belongs to a partial-bundle reconstruction that may be implicit.
body.consumer: A sufficient audited EHR design obtains standard errors for every treatment-specific endpoint probability on its regular identified strata.

obligation.what_is_open: The statistical limit follows on any regular branch once the population reconstruction is known to equal \(Q\); that equality is unavailable because constructive completeness is open.
obligation.obstruction: Continuous differentiability alone yields a limit centered at \(F(o)\). Identifying that center with the causal target requires the missing recovery theorem and cannot be inserted by definition.
obligation.attempted: I carried out the finite-multinomial continuity and delta-method reduction, including the fixed known-audit-probability linear composition, and isolated \(F(o)=Q\) as the only identification-dependent step.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on the unproved equality \(F(o)=Q\), the asymptotic argument
is complete.  The finite multinomial law gives
\[
\widehat o_n\longrightarrow o\quad\text{in probability},
\qquad
\sqrt n(\widehat o_n-o)
\Rightarrow N\!\left(0,\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top\right).
\]
Continuity of \(F\) gives consistency.  Continuous differentiability at
\(o\) and the multivariate delta method give
\[
\sqrt n\{F(\widehat o_n)-F(o)\}
\Rightarrow
N\!\left(0,
DF(o)[\operatorname{diag}(o)-oo^\top]DF(o)^\top\right).
\]
If the local extension is only defined on a neighborhood of \(o\), define
the estimator arbitrarily off that neighborhood; the probability of this
modification tends to zero.  Known-probability inverse-weighted pattern
tables are a fixed finite linear transform of the observed-cell histogram,
so composition with that transform gives the corresponding conclusion.
The unresolved identification theorem is needed solely to justify
\(F(o)=Q\) from \(\mathsf C=1\).
